title: TB PC-valid, private gpg key.asc, fails decrypting ONLY on TB mobile yet healthy on OpenKeyChain
creator: g8mxofj74
content:
Hi,

I have exported a from my Debian linux GnuPG private ed25519 keyring a private armor format private.asc file for upload into my mobile OpenKeyChain (showing healthy) and imported on my mobile thunderbird version 21.1 the private key from OpenKeyChain.

When receiving an encrypted email, my thunderbird PC version decrypts while my Mobile thunderbird show an error in decryption operation: I can read encrypted email on my PC, not on my mobile.

When I send a encrypted message From my mobile TB exact identical key to another of my email addresses, the email received into my mobile TB is automatically showing decrypted. This email is also decrypted on my PC thunderbird.

The TB account on both devices are the same. The private key is the same. The email provider is the same. The email addresses are identities of the the same key.

I have had this problem before. I have resolved this in the past and can no longer figure out how.

Any intuition? cheers.

title: Possible settings fault
creator: valjohnpics
content:
I have emailed 7th August to what appears on my mobile from Thunderbird settings just a review address. I explained that I have not received in Thunderbird any emails from my BT email system since Monday 22 July which happens to be the date shown on my mobile phone as the last date for your update. I can send emails via Thunderbird but not receive messages. The email address I use is john.morris@deritter.org.uk which goes to john.m280@btinternet.com I am sending this message from my laptop as it is easier to write that way and I stand a better chance of getting a reply than on my mobile Thunderbird.

Could you please let be know if your settings update on 22July caused the problem or what else needs putting right.

Another question. BT have a Spam folder to which many important emails are directed. These are not collected by Thunderbird which does not have a Spam folder. This means that if verifying codes are sent to my email address I can't recover them.

I am otherwise very pleased with Thunderbird and would just like these points investigated. Kind regards John Morris
